key: Make pleasant hymns, spin out your songs and praises: build ye a ship equipped with oars for transport. Prepare the implements, make all things ready, and let the sacrifice, my friends, go forward.
s: Calling friends to wake and kindle Agni, the hymn sets them working like farmers; Sāyaṇa, on 10.101.2, takes the ship as the piling of the fire altar, carried through by ploughing as by an oar, and the implements as ploughs and yokes.

evidence.gloss: Works (dhiyaḥ): the works of ploughing the site of the piling and the rest; spread them out. And make the ship that is to be carried across by an oar which takes the form of ploughing and the like: the ship called the piling (cayana). And make the weapons (āyudhā), the ploughs, yokes and the rest, ready.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok; ref Rig Veda 10.101.2 and at [937,2] match). Plain sense faithful to day.js: 10.101.1 bids the friends wake with one mind and kindle Agni, and the hymn goes on to ploughs, yokes, furrow, seed, sickle, well and buckets. Reading the whole commentary on 10.101: Sāyaṇa opens with the priests about to pile the fire speaking (on v.1), and at 10.101.2 glosses dhiyaḥ as the works of ploughing the site of the piling, the oar-driven ship as the ship called the piling, carried across by an oar that is ploughing and the like, and āyudhā as ploughs, yokes and the rest. Every element of the reading is in his words; Wilson follows (weapons, ship propelled by oars). Revision 368305 dated 2023-02-26 by the Wikisource API. Gate ok.
